claim: REQ-513's dispatch-guard (the FIND-103/FIND-201 fix) defines exactly TWO named routing branches for a rejected/fabricated slot — 'the BASELINE attempt' (routes into REQ-505's bounded-reprompt path) and 'the REROUTE attempt' (routes DIRECTLY into REQ-508's escalation, no third think() call) — but there is a real THIRD scenario neither branch unambiguously covers and which the spec's own acceptance criteria never test: a fabricated/off-menu slot (e.g. `slot:'sleep'`) returned on the RE-INVOKED think() call that REQ-505's own no-tool-call reprompt triggers (i.e. attempt #2 caused by REQ-505, as opposed to attempt #2 caused by REQ-506's reroute). REQ-504 point 5 (behavioral-spec.md:229-237) names only TWO possible values for `currentOfferedSlots` — `ctx.alwaysActMenu` for 'the baseline attempt' and REQ-506's narrower filtered array for 'a reroute attempt' — it never defines a distinct value/identity for 'the REQ-505 reprompt attempt'. Since REQ-505's reprompt does not narrow the tool schema (only REQ-506's reroute does), the reprompt attempt's `currentOfferedSlots` is, by the only definitions the spec gives, `ctx.alwaysActMenu` — IDENTICAL in array-identity to attempt #1's baseline value. REQ-513's EARS text (behavioral-spec.md:509-511) says: 'IF this is the BASELINE attempt (REQ-511's shared extra-call budget not yet spent), THE SYSTEM SHALL treat this exactly as a no-tool-call outcome for REQ-505's bounded-reprompt path' and defines 'BASELINE attempt' operationally via `currentOfferedSlots === ctx.alwaysActMenu` (REQ-504 point 5). A rejected slot arriving on the REQ-505 reprompt attempt satisfies that SAME array-identity test (`currentOfferedSlots === ctx.alwaysActMenu`) even though the shared extra-call budget IS already spent at that point (the reprompt call itself was the one shared extra call, per REQ-511's own edge case: 'once the shared budget's one extra call is spent (by either a reprompt or a reroute), no further reprompt/reroute is attempted this wake — REQ-508 escalates instead', behavioral-spec.md:447-451). This is a direct textual contradiction: REQ-513's own literal branch-selection rule (keyed on array identity) would route a reprompt-attempt-2 fabrication back into 'REQ-505's bounded-reprompt path' — which, read plainly by an implementer who has not internalized REQ-511's separate edge-case prose, means issuing a SECOND reprompt, i.e. a THIRD think() call overall — directly violating REQ-511's own hard, money-safety-critical 2-total ceiling (PROP-511a, verification-architecture.md:162, explicitly labeled 'money-safety-critical'). Nothing in REQ-505, REQ-511, or REQ-513 names a third `currentOfferedSlots`/attempt-identity value or an explicit rule distinguishing 'attempt #2 via reprompt, now rejected' from 'attempt #1, rejected' — the spec conflates them by array identity. This is exactly the same CLASS of ambiguity this spec pair has already been caught on twice (FIND-102: an off-by-one in the total-call ceiling's own wording; FIND-201: the dispatch guard checking the wrong reference array) — a third instance of the identical failure mode (an unbounded/miscounted think()-call path) has been reintroduced by REQ-513's own iteration-3 fix, in the one case its own acceptance criteria never test.

required_fix: REQ-513 must define a THIRD, unambiguous case (or, equivalently, replace its currentOfferedSlots-identity-based branch selection with an explicit attempt-budget-state check, matching REQ-511's own edge-case wording verbatim) so a rejected/fabricated slot on ANY attempt after the true first (baseline) attempt -- whether that second attempt was triggered by REQ-505's reprompt OR REQ-506's reroute -- routes DIRECTLY into REQ-508's escalation, never a third think() call. Concretely: thread an explicit attempt-budget flag (e.g. reuse `nextRerouteState`'s own `attemptsUsed`/`exhausted` output, already defined in Pure Core) into the dispatch guard's routing decision instead of (or in addition to) `currentOfferedSlots` identity, and rewrite REQ-513's EARS clause so the 'BASELINE attempt' branch is explicitly gated on 'attemptsUsed === 0' (the true first think() call of the wake), not merely on 'currentOfferedSlots === ctx.alwaysActMenu' (which a REQ-505 reprompt attempt also satisfies). Add a new acceptance criterion / PROP (e.g. PROP-513e) asserting: given a REQ-505 reprompt in flight (attempt #1 returned no tool call, attempt #2 is the reprompt, currentOfferedSlots===ctx.alwaysActMenu for attempt #2 exactly as for attempt #1), a parsed tool call on attempt #2 resolving to `{slot:'sleep', args:{}}` (or any slot absent from ctx.alwaysActMenu) is REJECTED and the wake proceeds DIRECTLY into REQ-508's escalation -- NOT a second reprompt / third think() call.
